backlog.spec: Add approximate pH 7.4 ionization features. Count carboxylic acids (existing ACID SMARTS), aliphatic amines (existing AMINE SMARTS), and quaternary or permanently charged nitrogens (SMARTS [N+;!$(N=O);!$(N-[O-])]). Compute an ionization penalty equal to 3.0 times the acid count plus 1.0 times the amine count capped at 1 per molecule, and then a logD proxy equal to MolLogP minus that penalty. Append the logD proxy, the penalty, the permanent charge count, and the net formal charge to the descriptor block fed to LightGBM. Keep the rest unchanged. This is a rule-based stand-in for the pH-dependent partitioning that governs passive permeability.
backlog.title: Ionization-corrected logD proxy features

backlog.spec: Set the LightGBM learning rate to 0.01 and n_estimators to 1500. Keep the other parameters and the L1 objective. The lower rate should give a smoother fit on the small dataset. Check that the 10 minute limit is not at risk.
backlog.title: Lower learning rate, longer boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the current convex blend (0.75 LightGBM + 0.25 Tanimoto kNN of the raw target) with a residual-correction scheme. First fit the existing descriptor-only LightGBM on all training rows and compute its out-of-fold residuals using an internal 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training molecules. Then run the same distance-weighted Tanimoto kNN (Morgan radius-2 2048 bits, k=7, inverse distance weights) on those out-of-fold residuals rather than on train_y, and return the full-data LightGBM prediction plus 0.5 times the kNN residual estimate. This lets the nearest-neighbour term only carry structural information the gradient boosting missed, instead of competing with it, which should help on folds where a test scaffold has one close analogue. Keep features and all LightGBM hyperparameters unchanged; the inner 5-fold refit multiplies runtime by about six, which is still far inside the budget.
backlog.title: kNN residual correction instead of prediction blending

backlog.spec: Compute each test molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to its k nearest training neighbours. Set the kNN weight per molecule to w = clip(0.1 + 0.6*(meansim-0.3), 0.1, 0.45), and use (1-w)*lgbm + w*knn. This gives kNN more weight on close analogues and less on novel scaffolds. Modify knn_predict to return the mean similarity too.
backlog.title: Local-similarity gated blend weight

backlog.spec: Fit TruncatedSVD with 20 components, using random_state=seed, on the training Morgan count fingerprints (1024 bits). Append the transformed components for train and test to the descriptor matrix given to LightGBM. Keep the kNN blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Morgan SVD components added to descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES of each training molecule with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold. Set the sample weight to 1/sqrt(cluster_size) and normalize the weights to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit. The aim is to reduce the dominance of large series in training, so generalisation to unseen scaffolds improves.
backlog.title: Scaffold-cluster inverse-size sample weights

backlog.spec: In featurize and morgan_bits, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest heavy-atom fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(m, asMols=True) and max by GetNumHeavyAtoms, then compute descriptors and fingerprints from that fragment. Fall back to the original molecule if parsing the fragment fails. Leave the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Correct the shrinkage that blending tends to introduce. Inside fit_predict, run a 4-fold inner KFold on the training molecules (shuffled with seed). For each inner fold, fit the existing LightGBM and kNN blend on the inner-train part and predict the inner-validation part. Collect the out-of-fold blended predictions for all training molecules and fit a least-absolute-deviation line y = a + b*pred (use scipy.optimize.minimize with the L1 loss, starting at a=0, b=1). Fit the full model on all training data, apply the blend to the test molecules, and then apply a and b to the output. Clip the output to the training range of train_y. Cost is about 5 times the current job time, so use n_estimators 300 to stay within the limit.
backlog.title: Post-hoc linear recalibration of blended predictions

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed n_estimators=500, choose the number of boosting rounds per fold by early stopping. Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into a 85/15 inner split using a seeded random split (seed from the argument), fit the L1 LightGBM with n_estimators=3000, learning_rate=0.03 and the current remaining hyperparameters using the inner holdout as eval_set with eval_metric='l1' and early_stopping_rounds=100, read off the best iteration, then refit a fresh model on the full training set with n_estimators set to round(best_iteration * 1.15) (clipped to [100, 3000]). Keep the final 0.75 GBM / 0.25 Tanimoto kNN blend unchanged. This adapts the boosting length to each fold instead of using one global guess.
backlog.title: Inner early stopping for tree count

backlog.spec: Keep the architecture and blend fixed and only add LightGBM's small-data regularizers to the existing L1 model: set max_bin=63 (fewer, coarser histogram bins), path_smooth=10.0 (shrinks leaf values toward their parent), min_child_samples=15, and feature_fraction_bynode=0.5 while removing colsample_bytree (set it to 1.0 so the per-node fraction is the only column sampling). Leave n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed. The final prediction stays 0.75 * LightGBM + 0.25 * Tanimoto kNN. These knobs attack the main failure mode on 728 rows with ~210 descriptors, namely leaves fit on very few molecules.
backlog.title: Small-data LightGBM smoothing knobs

backlog.spec: Add a small set of charge descriptors to the descriptor block. Using rdkit.Chem.AllChem.ComputeGasteigerCharges on each molecule (after Chem.AddHs is not needed), compute the max and min partial charge over heavy atoms, their sum of absolute values, the sum of positive charges, the sum of negative charges, and the charge span (max minus min). Also add the count of heavy atoms with |charge| > 0.2. Append these 7 numbers to the descriptor block before LightGBM, with NaN and inf replaced by 0. Leave the Morgan part and kNN unchanged. Charge features relate to the polarity that drives passive permeability.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge statistics as features

backlog.spec: Augment the training set for the LightGBM only. After building the training descriptor matrix, compute each column's training standard deviation, then create two extra noisy copies of the whole training block by adding Gaussian noise of 0.05 * column_sd (drawn with a numpy Generator seeded from the seed argument) to every column, stacking the original and the two jittered copies into one training matrix of 3x the rows with the labels tiled accordingly. Fit the existing L1 LightGBM on this augmented set with no other hyperparameter changes, predict on the clean test descriptors, and keep the final 0.75 GBM / 0.25 Tanimoto kNN blend. The jitter blurs the exact split thresholds the trees can choose, acting like input-noise regularization for a 728-row dataset while runtime stays small.
backlog.title: Gaussian descriptor jitter augmentation

backlog.spec: Keep the current pipeline (RDKit 2D descriptor block, L1-style LightGBM, 0.75/0.25 blend with the Tanimoto kNN) but enable LightGBM's linear_tree=True so each leaf fits a ridge-regularized linear model of the features instead of a constant. Because many Caco-2-relevant descriptors (TPSA, logP, MW, HBD counts) relate to permeability in a near-linear fashion, linear leaves can extrapolate to unseen scaffolds better than piecewise constants. Use linear_tree=True together with linear_lambda=1.0, reduce num_leaves to about 8 and n_estimators to about 300 since linear leaves are far more expressive per split, and keep learning_rate, subsample, colsample_bytree, random_state=seed and n_jobs=8. If LightGBM errors on NaN or infinite feature values with linear trees, rely on the existing nan_to_num and clipping in featurize, and additionally cast the descriptor matrix to float64 contiguous before fitting.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM on descriptors

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, first fit a Ridge regression (alpha about 10) on standardized inputs. Use the RDKit descriptor block (nd columns) and fit it to train_y. Compute the in-sample residuals train_y minus the ridge prediction, and fit the existing L1 LightGBM on those residuals with the same descriptor features. For test molecules, the final prediction is the ridge prediction plus the LightGBM residual prediction. Keep the kNN blend at 0.25 and the rest unchanged. The aim is to let trees model what a linear logP/TPSA/MW trend cannot extrapolate.
backlog.title: Linear baseline plus LightGBM on residuals

backlog.spec: Add ring-topology features derived from the Murcko scaffold. For each molecule, compute the Murcko scaffold with MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol, count ring systems (connected groups of rings sharing atoms), the size of the largest ring system in heavy atoms, the number of fused ring junctions (atoms shared by two or more rings), the number of spiro atoms, the fraction of heavy atoms that are in the scaffold, and the number of acyclic heavy atoms. Append these 6 numbers to the descriptor block for the L1 LightGBM. Leave the Morgan kNN and the blend weights unchanged.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold size features

backlog.spec: For each molecule, add hydrogens, embed one conformer with ETKDG using randomSeed set from the seed argument, and run a light MMFF optimization with maxIters 200 (fall back to no optimization if it fails, and to zeros if embedding fails). Compute rdMolDescriptors PMI1, PMI2, PMI3, NPR1, NPR2, radius of gyration, and asphericity, and append these 7 values to the descriptor block for LightGBM. Remove hydrogens before the existing 2D descriptors are computed so that they are unchanged. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same. Cap the total runtime by using a fixed seed and no retries.
backlog.title: Three-dimensional shape descriptors from a seeded conformer

backlog.spec: The incumbent uses RDKit 2D descriptors only, because raw Morgan count columns (2048 sparse features) diluted the gradient boosting. Instead, compress the structural information: build the Morgan radius-2 count fingerprint (1024 bits, as the existing featurize helper already does), fit sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD(n_components=32, random_state=seed) on the training fingerprint matrix only, and append the 32 transformed components to the descriptor block for both train and test (transform test with the training-fitted SVD, never refit on test). Feed this descriptors-plus-32-components matrix to the unchanged LightGBM and keep the 0.75/0.25 kNN blend as is. Dense low-rank substructure axes are cheap for trees to split on and avoid the sparsity problem that sank the raw-count variant.
backlog.title: Truncated-SVD components of Morgan counts appended to descriptors

backlog.spec: The current script fits a single LightGBM regressor (L1/Huber objective, 500 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10) on the RDKit 2D descriptor block only, then blends 0.75 LightGBM + 0.25 Tanimoto kNN. Make one minimal hyperparameter step: set num_leaves=31 and min_child_samples=20, leaving every other setting, the feature block and the blend untouched. The intent is to test whether the tree capacity is slightly under-fit on 580-molecule training folds while keeping leaf population large enough to stay stable under scaffold-held-out folds. Change only the two keyword arguments in the LGBMRegressor constructor; do not add new code paths, extra models, or feature columns. Keep random_state=seed and n_jobs=8.
backlog.title: Finer LightGBM capacity step: 31 leaves, min_child_samples 20

backlog.spec: Before fitting, smooth the training labels: for each training molecule compute the distance-weighted Tanimoto kNN estimate of its own label from the other training molecules only (Morgan radius-2 2048 bits, k=7, exclude self by masking the diagonal of the train-train distance matrix), then replace train_y by y_smooth = 0.85 * y + 0.15 * y_neighbour. Fit the existing L1 LightGBM on the smoothed labels, keep the kNN test prediction computed from the original (unsmoothed) train_y, and keep the final 0.75/0.25 blend. Measured Caco-2 values carry assay noise; shrinking each label slightly toward its chemical neighbourhood should reduce the variance the trees fit, without changing features or model family.
backlog.title: Neighbour label smoothing of the target

backlog.spec: Keep the L1 LightGBM on descriptors but replace the constant learning rate with a decaying schedule. Use n_estimators 1000 and pass callbacks=[lgb.reset_parameter(learning_rate=...)] to fit, where the learning rate at iteration i equals 0.05 times (0.1 raised to i/1000), so it decays smoothly from 0.05 to about 0.005. Keep num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.5, subsample 0.8, min_child_samples 10 and the L1 objective. The kNN blend stays at 0.25. The change is only in the learning-rate schedule and the number of rounds.
backlog.title: Decaying learning-rate schedule for LightGBM

memo:
Incumbent is slot 17: L1 LightGBM on RDKit 2D descriptors blended with kNN, mean_adjusted 0.3694 over 2 runs (0.3725/0.3664).

Helped: data/feature changes (descriptors + Morgan counts 0.3781; kNN blend 0.3976) and the switch to L1 LightGBM on descriptors (-0.0086).

Did not help: family swaps (SVR 0.4222, CatBoost 0.4102, RF 0.3953), feature additions (MACCS+atom-pair 0.3836, Crippen/EState 0.3728, EState fingerprint 0.3716, MACCS 0.3703), pruning (0.3797), winsorizing (0.3792), bagging/subsampled LightGBM (0.3709, 0.3764, 0.3923), stronger regularization (0.3761), min-max kNN (0.3793), kernel ridge (0.3740), DART (4.0173). XGBoost runs failed (94.3105).

Small blends (SVR 0.3693, atom-pair 0.3686, Huber 0.3691) are within the noise sd of about 0.0037.

Next: gains are near the noise floor. Try only small LightGBM tweaks (leaves, learning rate) and small kNN weight/k steps. Replicate any candidate before accepting. Avoid more family swaps, feature additions and pruning.
